thesis: Finite verifiable worlds reveal exactly what evidence licenses and why bridges from models to nature matter.
role: Consolidates the method through complete toy examples and research proposals.

ideas.statement: An incomplete observed state can make deterministic behavior look inconsistent without disproving determinism.
A conserved quantity in a finite ring does not become energy or life by being renamed.
External pauses can change an external counter while preserving identical internal evidence under explicit isolation.
Research must expose predictions, alternatives and costs of error; distributed verification requires responsible institutions.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: The finite ring is reversible and conserves the number of ones, with all states enumerated.
A hidden binary state changes the successor of the same visible value.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Toy worlds contain no conscious observers; they do not refute Bell results or establish actual cosmic pauses.
Benefiting from a definition does not prove deliberate design, while lack of intent does not remove unequal effects.

audit.notes: Every unit read. Glossary treated as consolidation; all numerical worlds remain explicitly educational.
